concept.name: Piercing line
concept.definition: A two-candlestick pattern in a downtrend: a long black candle is followed by a white candle that opens below the prior low (ideally with a gap) and closes more than halfway up into the prior black body. Technical analysts read it as a potential bottom reversal signal, a weaker cousin of the bullish engulfing pattern.
concept.intuition: Sellers gapped the market down at the open, but buyers drove price back up through more than half of the previous session's losses, piercing deep into their territory.
concept.mechanics: From OHLC data: candle 1 is a long black body; candle 2 opens at or below L1 and closes above the midpoint (O1 + C1) / 2 of the first body but below O1 (otherwise it would be a bullish engulfing). The deeper the close into the first body, the stronger the conventional reading.
concept.formula: Piercing line when C1 < O1, O2 <= L1, and (O1 + C1)/2 < C2 < O1.
concept.failure_modes: A close that only just passes the midpoint is weak and often fails, especially in strong downtrends. On 24-hour markets like forex where gaps are rare, the opening-gap requirement is often relaxed, which dilutes the pattern.
concept.misconceptions: Closing above the prior candle's high or open turns it into an engulfing pattern, not a piercing line; the close must stop within the first body. It is also not a confirmed reversal without follow-through.
concept.example: A stock falls, printing a candle from 44.00 open to 42.00 close (low 41.80). The next day opens at 41.50 and closes at 43.50, above the 43.00 midpoint of the prior body: a piercing line that bulls read as a bottoming attempt.
